reading.body:
Microsoft EAT02 is one of the oldest hyperscale campuses in North America, established around 2007 as part of Microsoft's Central Washington region. Its exact power capacity and physical footprint are not published by Microsoft, which discloses only worldwide aggregate statistics across 80+ Azure regions and does not release facility-level specifications for individual campuses. The campus sits within Douglas County in a dual-county data center hub that has transformed the region since the early 2000s, with substantial local public coverage and a dedicated Microsoft community page documenting its expansion.

Washington State has 46 mapped data center facilities, of which only two operators publish power capacity figures at the individual campus level. EAT02 ranks third among published capacity in the state, though it contributes no disclosed megawatts to that ranking because Microsoft does not publish its own power draw. The two facilities with published figures account for 60 MW of the state's total disclosed capacity, leaving the vast majority of mapped capacity, including this campus, opaque in terms of actual power demand.

Without published specifications, EAT02 cannot be sized against the scaling constraints that matter to AI deployment: power draw, PUE efficiency rating, cooling availability, or grid interconnection capacity. Its age and position in Microsoft's most mature hyperscale region suggest operational significance to the operator, but the absence of disclosed figures means this campus cannot be evaluated using the metrics that determine whether a data center matters to AI scaling in the published record.
